text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
LIETUVOS RYTAS

- Chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbergis met U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington and discussed security issues. Landsbergis said the promise to keep the doors of NATO open was not enough since they might remain open for an indefinite time.
- The Centre Union initiated discussions in parliament on a constitutional amendment which would allow Lithuanians living abroad to be a candidate for president.
- Homeland Union member Rolandas Paksas, 41, was elected as mayor of Vilnius municipality.
- It is expected that a special group to investigate financial fraud cases will be formed.
- Hermis Bank reported 9.3 million litas net profit in the first quarter of 1997.
- Klaipeda transport fleet boosted its share capital by 15 million litas from profit reserves to 101 million litas.
RESPUBLIKA
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said excise duties on alcohol and oil products will continue to rise until they reach the same level as in central European states.
- The EMI record company, on the advise of Mstislav Rostropovich, suggested that Landsbergis record a CD with Mikalojus Chiurlionis sonatas for piano in the famous Abbey Road studio in London.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- Vagnorius said that his government will not borrow any more to pay for energy resourses.

- Lithuania and Latvia continued negotiations over the disputed territory in the Baltic sea in Vilnius. Politicians said there seems to be some hope of a compromise in the talks, which hit a wall last autumn.
VERSLO ZINIOS

- Algis Avizhienis, the head of Lithuania's Investment Agency, has resigned on the grounds that the PHARE program cut its financing. Another reason for his resignation was the decision to merge the institution with the Export Promotion Agency.
- The government expects that the increase of excise taxes on alcohol, tobacco and oil products will add 300 million litas rto state evenues.
- Industrial financial group Status asked dealers to sell its 53 percent share in pharmaceutical producer Sanitas and its 70 percent share in Vilnius Tauras brewery.
- Lithuanian officials expect that after the third round of talks on April 13-15 a free trade agreement between Lithuania and Turkey will be signed.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom + 370 2 22 35 17
